projects.description: This 36-month programme supports the designation and operationalization of the Makgadikgadi Landscape in Botswana as a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. The project strengthens institutional governance, develops integrated management and business plans, and builds national and local capacity under the MAB framework. It combines ecosystem restoration, biodiversity monitoring, and climate resilience measures with community-based economic development, targeting women and youth through sustainable value chains and cooperative support. By integrating conservation, local livelihoods, and scientific monitoring tools such as GIS, the programme aims to enhance ecological integrity while fostering inclusive and resilient development in one of Botswana’s most ecologically significant landscapes.

projects.name: Advancing Social Protection and Employment Opportunities in Botswana
projects.description:
During 2026 the ILO in collaboration with with UNICEF, UNDP and other agencies  will seek to explore multiple opportunities for improving efficiency of the social protection system, including implementation of the Single Social Registry, improving targeting and data management, more efficient benefit delivery systems, strengthening case management, and reallocating spending to programs that have the greatest impact on reducing poverty. The limited effectiveness of Active Labor Market Programs and youth employment initiatives to promote labor market inclusion is largely due to weaknesses in program design and concept, inadequate training and intermediation support, and persistent implementation challenges. In a context of fiscal constraints, addressing these gaps is a priority.
Therefore, this  Joint Programme will focus on strengthening the SP systems to be more efficient in service delivery, rationalizing of social protection expenditures, and fostering an evidence-based ecosystem initiatives for enhancing economic opportunities for youth and poor.

projects.name: GEF-BDLD.10958. Strengthening national-level institutional and professional capacities of country Parties towards enhanced UNCCD monitoring and reporting – GEF 7 EA Umbrella IV
projects.description:
The international community through the UN member states adopted, in September 2015, the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development with 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Among these SDGs, Goal 15 is particularly relevant for the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD). Through this goal, countries are urged to, Protect, restore and promote sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems, sustainably manage forests, combat desertification, and halt and reverse land degradation and halt biodiversity loss. The target 15.3 urges countries to combat desertification, restore degraded land and soil, including land affected by desertification, drought and floods, and strive
to achieve a land degradation-neutral world by 2030.
The twelfth session of the Conference of Parties (COP.12) of the UNCCD agreed in October 2015 to integrate the SDGs and related targets into the implementation of the Convention and decided that striving to achieve SDG target 15.3 is a strong vehicle for driving implementation of the UNCCD (decision 3/COP.12). COP.12 also endorsed the definition of land degradation neutrality (LDN) and invited Parties to (i) formulate voluntary targets to achieve LDN, (ii) use the UNCCD monitoring and evaluation framework, including progress indicators, to monitor, evaluate and communicate progress towards achieving the LDN target, (iii) explore options on how to integrate the voluntary LDN targets in their UNCCD National Action Programmes (NAPs), and (iv) promote the use of LDN targets and projects and other SLM initiatives as an effective vehicle for mobilizing additional sustainable financing and investments to address issues related to desertification, land degradation and drought (DLDD). LDN has therefore become an important, while non mandatory, element of UNCCD implementation, while at the same time contributing to other SDGs, including those SDGs relating to climate change mitigation and adaptation, biodiversity conservation, ecosystem restoration, food and
water security, disaster risk reduction, and poverty reduction.
Decision 2/COP.12 invites affected country Parties to establish national baselines and national-level voluntary LDN targets within their National Action Plans (NAPs). The New 10-year strategic plan and framework to enhance the implementation of the Convention paves the way for an enhanced reporting and review process within the UNCCD that considers the SDG framework. As such, UNCCD reporting and review system is based on (i) progress indicators to measure the progress against the future strategic framework of the UNCCD, and (ii) an implementation framework to assess actions at national and sub-national level relevant for UNCCD implementation. The reporting and review system addresses effective monitoring of financing for UNCCD implementation using refined methodologies in accordance with COP decisions.

projects.description:
Technical Assistance for Botswana’s Voluntary National GCM Review
The UN Network on Migration, with EU-funded support, will assist Botswana in preparing its voluntary national review of the Global Compact for Migration (GCM) ahead of the 2026 International Migration Review Forum. This process will assess progress, identify gaps, and set priorities for safe, orderly, and regular migration. Activities include an inception workshop, targeted questionnaires, progress assessment, multi-stakeholder consultations, drafting and validation of the review, and visibility efforts. The initiative is co-designed with the government to ensure inclusivity and data-driven outcomes within a EUR 10,000 budget.

projects.name: Enhanced institutional capacities of national partners to produce, compile and use the tools provided to promote decent work.
projects.description: Botswana, through Statistics Botswana, conducted the Household Income and Expenditure Survey named Botswana Multi-Topic Household Survey (BMTHS). The survey takes a year to be completed. Data collection ran from November 2024 to Mid-October 2025. In 2024, the ILO supported Statistics Botswana to incorporate the 19th ICLS in this non-Labour Force Survey (LFS) source, as well as informality. As Botswana has already adhered to the 19th ICLS in the Quarterly Labour Force Survey (QLFS), it was important to ensure that the standard is also applied in the BMTHS, so that the labour market indicators compiled in QLFS are comparable to the labour market indicators compiled in this BMTHS. Furthermore, the BMTHS is used to produce poverty indicators. Given the relationship between employment (or lack of) and poverty, it is essential that employment is well defined in BMTHS, to examine the relationship between poverty and employment in Botswana. Furthermore, this source will allow Botswana to report on SDG 1.1.1 (Working poverty rate), again, highlighting the reason why employment should be well defined in HIES. Statistics Botswana  has requested ILO support for data analysis and report on the labour market indicators from this source. The above is expected to contribute towards improved labour modules in other statistical sources, by introducing the new standards adopted by the International Conference of Labour Statisticians (ICLS). During 2026 the ILO will provided supported Botswana to produce a thematic report on the experience of youth in the labour market. This report is almost ready for dissemination and ILO is expected to provide support for the dissemination of this report.
projects.outcome: Increased availability and use of high-quality, disaggregated data by a more diverse range of stakeholders
